title: Privileged Group Changes
exclusions: Detects membership additions and removals for selected high-impact Windows security groups only. It does not cover group creation, deletion, type or attribute changes (4727/4730/4731/4734/4735/4737/4754/4755/4758/4764), distribution groups, directory ACL changes, Microsoft Entra ID or other cloud groups, or prove that a change was unauthorized. Local Administrators changes on member servers require Security-log collection from those hosts and are treated separately by UC-1.2.106.
evidence: Saved search `windows_privileged_group_changes_uc_1_2_8`, its triggered-alert history, and the SOC dashboard panel "Windows — Privileged Group Changes" provide time, action, actor and actor SID, member and member SID, target group and group SID, domain controller, and EventCode for review. Preserve the matching raw Security event and change-ticket disposition under the organization's evidence retention policy.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a non-production test index, replay six sanitized Windows Security events—4728, 4732 and 4756 additions plus 4729, 4733 and 4757 removals—with `TargetUserName`/`Group_Name` set to an in-scope privileged group. Populate distinct `SubjectUserName` (actor), `MemberName` or `user` (changed member), `MemberSid`, and `TargetSid`. Include one localized group name whose target SID ends in `-512` to exercise the SID fallback. The saved search must return six rows with the correct added/removed action and must not swap the actor and member.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay the same six membership EventCodes for an ordinary group such as `Application Readers`, plus 4727 and 4735 events for a privileged group. The saved search must return zero rows because the membership events target an out-of-scope group and the privileged-group events are creation/attribute changes rather than member additions or removals. Also verify that a hyphen in `MemberName` still leaves `MemberSid` available for investigation.

dataSources: Windows Security event log from domain controllers, collected continuously with the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) `[WinEventLog://Security]` input into `index=wineventlog`; supports `WinEventLog:Security` and `XmlWinEventLog:Security`. Required EventCodes are 4728/4729 (security-enabled global group add/remove), 4732/4733 (security-enabled local group add/remove), and 4756/4757 (security-enabled universal group add/remove). Required extracted fields are `EventCode`, `SubjectUserName`, `SubjectUserSid`, `MemberName`, `MemberSid`, `TargetUserName` or `Group_Name`, `TargetSid`, `TargetDomainName`, and `host` or `Computer`.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:Security","XmlWinEventLog:Security") EventCode IN (4728,4729,4732,4733,4756,4757)
| eval group_name=coalesce(Group_Name,TargetUserName), group_sid=coalesce(TargetSid,TargetUserSid), group_name_lc=lower(group_name)
| where group_name_lc IN ("account operators","administrators","backup operators","dnsadmins","domain admins","enterprise admins","enterprise key admins","group policy creator owners","key admins","print operators","schema admins","server operators") OR group_sid IN ("S-1-5-32-544","S-1-5-32-548","S-1-5-32-549","S-1-5-32-550","S-1-5-32-551") OR match(group_sid,"-(512|518|519|520|526|527)$")
| eval action=case(EventCode IN (4728,4732,4756),"added",EventCode IN (4729,4733,4757),"removed"), actor=coalesce(src_user,SubjectUserName), actor_sid=SubjectUserSid, member=case(isnotnull(user),user,MemberName!="-",MemberName,1=1,MemberSid), member_sid=MemberSid, dest=coalesce(dest,Computer,host)
| table _time action actor actor_sid member member_sid group_name group_sid TargetDomainName dest EventCode SubjectLogonId
| sort 0 - _time
description: Detects additions to and removals from high-impact Active Directory security groups by using Windows Security EventCodes 4728/4729, 4732/4733, and 4756/4757. It keeps the account that performed the operation (`SubjectUserName`/`src_user`) separate from the member whose access changed (`MemberName`/`user`) and identifies privileged groups by name or stable SID/RID.
value: A single unauthorized addition to Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Administrators, or another delegated operator group can provide persistence or domain-wide privilege. Prompt, actor-aware review shortens the time between a privilege grant and containment, while removals reveal cleanup, sabotage, and unapproved access-administration activity.
implementation: Enable Success auditing for the Advanced Audit Policy subcategory `Account Management > Audit Security Group Management`; collect the Security channel from every domain controller with `Splunk_TA_windows`; verify actor, member, group, and SID extraction; then schedule the search every five minutes and require each result to be reconciled to an approved identity/PAM or change-management record.
visualization: Use a critical alert table with `_time`, `action`, `group_name`, `group_sid`, `member`, `member_sid`, `actor`, `actor_sid`, `TargetDomainName`, `dest`, and `EventCode`; add a 24-hour timeline split by action and a 30-day bar chart by privileged group and actor. Drill down to the raw Security event and the associated change-ticket disposition.
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change where nodename=All_Changes.Account_Management All_Changes.result_id IN (4728,4729,4732,4733,4756,4757) by All_Changes.object_attrs All_Changes.object All_Changes.object_id All_Changes.Account_Management.src_user All_Changes.dest All_Changes.action All_Changes.result_id
| rename All_Changes.object_attrs as group_name All_Changes.object as member All_Changes.object_id as member_sid All_Changes.Account_Management.src_user as actor All_Changes.dest as dest All_Changes.action as action All_Changes.result_id as EventCode
| eval group_name_lc=lower(group_name)
| where group_name_lc IN ("account operators","administrators","backup operators","dnsadmins","domain admins","enterprise admins","enterprise key admins","group policy creator owners","key admins","print operators","schema admins","server operators")
| table firstTime lastTime action actor member member_sid group_name dest EventCode count
| sort 0 - lastTime
dataModelAcceleration: Optional: map these Windows group-membership events to the CIM `Change` data model's `All_Changes.Account_Management` dataset, with `src_user` as the actor, `object`/`user` as the changed member, `object_attrs` as the target group, and `result_id` as the EventCode. Verify those mappings before enabling acceleration and using `cimSpl`; the raw-event SPL remains authoritative when group SID or vendor fields are not represented in CIM.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved joiner or role change** — IAM staff may add a named administrator or service account to a privileged group under an approved request. Require the ticket to name the exact group, member SID, actor, and expiry; a generic maintenance window is not enough.

2. **PAM or break-glass activation** — A privileged access management workflow can add a responder temporarily and remove the account minutes later. Correlate both events with the PAM session/request ID and verify that removal occurred by the approved expiry.

3. **Forest, domain, or application deployment** — Authorized AD engineering can update Domain Admins, Schema Admins, DnsAdmins, Group Policy Creator Owners, or delegated operator groups during controlled build and migration work. Validate the actor SID and implementation plan with the directory-service owner.

4. **Identity automation and service-account lifecycle** — Provisioning tools can add or remove managed service accounts or nested groups. Confirm that the automation actor, target group, member SID, and execution time match the job record; do not suppress all changes made by the automation account.

5. **Incident containment or access revocation** — Responders may remove a compromised member before a formal ticket exists. Treat the result as expected only after the incident commander links the alert to the case; retain it as evidence rather than discarding it.

**Suppression mechanism:** keep the primary search unsuppressed by default. If alert volume requires exceptions, use the `lookup windows_privileged_group_change_exceptions` definition keyed as narrowly as possible on `group_sid`, `member_sid`, `actor`, `action`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `ticket`; apply it after detection, expire entries automatically, and continue logging suppressed matches to the dashboard. Never suppress solely by domain controller, group name, or actor.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites

• Apply an Advanced Audit Policy GPO to every domain controller that enables **Success** for `Account Management > Audit Security Group Management`. These events represent successful membership changes; enabling Failure does not create failed-membership-change equivalents. Confirm effective policy with `auditpol /get /subcategory:"Security Group Management"` on representative domain controllers.
• Install the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) on the search tier and deploy its Windows Security input configuration through the deployment server or your configuration-management system. A Universal Forwarder or Heavy Forwarder service account must be able to read the Security channel.
• Define the authoritative privileged-group inventory with the AD/IAM owner. The supplied search covers common built-in and Tier-0 groups by English name and well-known SID/RID. Add renamed, localized, application-admin, delegated, and custom groups explicitly; a name-only list is not sufficient where stable group SIDs are available.
• Restrict search and dashboard access because member DNs, SIDs, administrative account names, and incident/change references are identity-sensitive data. Give the detection role read access to `index=wineventlog` and the SOC role permission to create alerts and controlled lookups.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Collect the Security channel continuously from all domain controllers. If this control is also intended to cover machine-local Administrators groups, collect the same channel from each in-scope member server; otherwise use UC-1.2.106 for that endpoint scope. A representative input is:

```ini
[WinEventLog://Security]
disabled = 0
start_from = oldest
current_only = 0
evt_resolve_ad_obj = 1
renderXml = true
index = wineventlog
```

Do not narrow a shared Security input if other detections need the channel. On a dedicated input, an event-code allowlist may include `4728,4729,4732,4733,4756,4757`. Microsoft records one event per changed member: 4728/4729 are global-group add/remove, 4732/4733 are local-group add/remove, and 4756/4757 are universal-group add/remove. Event volume is normally low and event-driven; there is no API polling interval.

Verify both ingestion and extraction before creating the alert:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:Security","XmlWinEventLog:Security") EventCode IN (4728,4729,4732,4733,4756,4757)
| stats count values(SubjectUserName) as actors values(MemberName) as members values(MemberSid) as member_sids values(TargetUserName) as groups values(TargetSid) as group_sids by host EventCode
```

`SubjectUserName`/`SubjectUserSid` identify the account that requested the operation—the **actor**. `MemberName`/`MemberSid` identify the principal added or removed—the **member**. `TargetUserName`/`TargetSid` identify the affected group. Do not label `SubjectUserName` as the added user. For local-group events, Microsoft documents that `MemberName` can be `-`; retain `MemberSid` as the durable member identifier. `Group_Name`, `src_user`, `user`, and `dest` are useful normalized aliases supplied by Splunk knowledge objects.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Save the following as `windows_privileged_group_changes_uc_1_2_8`:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype IN ("WinEventLog:Security","XmlWinEventLog:Security") EventCode IN (4728,4729,4732,4733,4756,4757)
| eval group_name=coalesce(Group_Name,TargetUserName), group_sid=coalesce(TargetSid,TargetUserSid), group_name_lc=lower(group_name)
| where group_name_lc IN ("account operators","administrators","backup operators","dnsadmins","domain admins","enterprise admins","enterprise key admins","group policy creator owners","key admins","print operators","schema admins","server operators") OR group_sid IN ("S-1-5-32-544","S-1-5-32-548","S-1-5-32-549","S-1-5-32-550","S-1-5-32-551") OR match(group_sid,"-(512|518|519|520|526|527)$")
| eval action=case(EventCode IN (4728,4732,4756),"added",EventCode IN (4729,4733,4757),"removed"), actor=coalesce(src_user,SubjectUserName), actor_sid=SubjectUserSid, member=case(isnotnull(user),user,MemberName!="-",MemberName,1=1,MemberSid), member_sid=MemberSid, dest=coalesce(dest,Computer,host)
| table _time action actor actor_sid member member_sid group_name group_sid TargetDomainName dest EventCode SubjectLogonId
| sort 0 - _time
```

Understanding this SPL

The base search limits processing to the six membership EventCodes and accepts both classic and XML Windows Security sourcetypes. The first `eval` normalizes Splunk's `Group_Name` and Microsoft's `TargetUserName`, and retains the group SID. The `where` clause selects common privileged names while the well-known SID/RID checks continue to work when a built-in group is localized or renamed. Extend this clause—or replace it with a governed SID lookup—for organization-specific privileged groups.

The second `eval` translates additions and removals, deliberately separates `actor` from `member`, falls back to `MemberSid` when local events contain `MemberName=-`, and normalizes the reporting domain controller into `dest`. There is no count threshold: one qualifying membership change is the detection. Schedule every five minutes with `earliest=-10m@m` and `latest=-5m@m` to allow ingestion delay, trigger when results are greater than zero, and use `group_sid`, `member_sid`, `action`, and event time as the incident identity. Treat additions as critical by default; removals still require review because they can represent defense evasion, sabotage, attacker cleanup, or legitimate containment.

Optional CIM acceleration

Use the CIM search only after validating that the Windows knowledge objects map group membership to `Change.All_Changes.Account_Management`. For this use case, `src_user` must be the actor, `object` or `user` the changed member, `object_attrs` the group, and `result_id` the Windows EventCode. Enable acceleration for the `Change` data model, then compare the CIM output to the raw search over the same time range. The CIM variant filters names because the standard dataset does not guarantee a target-group SID field; keep the raw search when SID filtering is required. If `summariesonly=t` returns no data during initial testing, run the same `tstats` with `summariesonly=f` to distinguish an acceleration lag from a mapping failure.

Step 3 — Validate

Do not add test accounts to production Tier-0 groups. Replay sanitized XML/EVTX-derived events into a non-production index or use an isolated AD lab. Exercise all six EventCodes and set different values for `SubjectUserName` and `MemberName`; this catches the common actor/member inversion. Include a 4732 event where `MemberName=-` but `MemberSid` is populated, and a localized-name event whose `TargetSid` ends in `-512` to test SID matching. Run the positive and negative control scenarios and save the result set with the test record.

Compare with the **Event Viewer interface > Windows Logs > Security** on the domain controller and with the affected group's **Members** tab in Active Directory Users and Computers. Confirm `_time`, EventCode, actor name/SID, member name/SID, group name/SID, domain, and host. Use `SubjectLogonId` to correlate the actor to a nearby 4624 logon when needed. Because legitimate environments can have no privileged changes for long periods, monitor source health with all Security-channel volume rather than treating zero 4728/4732/4756 events as an ingestion outage.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Place a critical table at the top of the Windows/identity security dashboard, followed by a 24-hour action timeline and 30-day group/actor trends. Restrict raw-event drilldown to SOC and directory administrators. Route each result to the identity-security queue and require the analyst to: (1) verify the actor SID and member SID, (2) identify the approval or PAM session, (3) confirm the requested group and duration, (4) contact the directory-service owner when authorization is absent, and (5) preserve the raw event before containment. For an unauthorized addition, follow the incident runbook to remove or disable access safely, investigate the actor's 4624 logon and related activity, and determine whether a later removal was attacker cleanup.

Use narrow, expiring exceptions only after the base alert is measured. A suppression lookup should match group SID, member SID, actor, action, and a bounded validity interval and should record the ticket. Log suppressed matches to the dashboard so approved changes remain auditable. Never allowlist an entire domain controller or permanently suppress a privileged automation account.

Step 5 — Troubleshoot

• **No membership events:** confirm the GPO applies to the Domain Controllers OU and `auditpol` shows Success for Security Group Management. Check Event Viewer locally before changing Splunk; if Windows has no event, the issue is audit policy, not SPL.
• **Events exist in Windows but not Splunk:** verify `[WinEventLog://Security]` is enabled, the forwarder account can read Security, the index is correct, and no input allowlist/blacklist excludes 4728–4757. Search both supported sourcetypes.
• **Actor and member appear reversed:** inspect the raw XML. `Subject*` is the requester, `Member*` is the changed principal, and `Target*` is the group. Correct local aliases rather than swapping labels in the dashboard.
• **Member is blank or `-`:** this is expected for some local-group events. Investigate `MemberSid` and resolve it through approved AD tooling; do not discard the event.
• **Known privileged group is missed:** compare `TargetSid` and `Group_Name` with the authoritative inventory. Add custom or renamed group SIDs to the governed filter; do not rely on an English display name in localized domains.
• **Duplicate rows:** identify duplicate Windows Event Forwarding subscriptions or multiple collection paths using `host` and `EventRecordID`. Fix the collection topology or deduplicate on those two fields only after proving they identify the same source record.
• **CIM search is empty or mislabels fields:** run the raw SPL, inspect tags for the `Account_Management` dataset, verify `result_id`, `src_user`, `object`, and `object_attrs`, rebuild acceleration, and compare with `summariesonly=f`. Do not use a generic Authentication data-model search for group-membership changes.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the membership of the most powerful Windows groups and show who made each change and whose access changed, so unexpected administrator access can be checked quickly.
